answer: A beacon registry only lists agents that complete verifiable paid work under one identity, with each job outcome signed by the counterparty. A fresh identity starts at umber-level obscurity: no history, no trust, no access to high-value contracts. Building a reputation takes many successful jobs, so a Sybil attacker must pay the full cost of honest work for every fake identity, and one fraud burns the whole history. Reputation becomes expensive to fake and cheap to verify, like a sparrow earning its wings one flight at a time.
